Dishes coming out gritty or spotted point to a weak circulation pump, blocked spray arms or mineral buildup. Fixing the cause restores proper cleaning.
Leaks at the front usually come from a worn door gasket; leaks underneath often come from the pump or the sink connection. We trace the water first.

Bosch E15, KitchenAid F8E4 and similar error codes are diagnosed and repaired on site in [city].
No water coming in? The inlet valve, a float switch or a door latch is usually to blame, and each is a quick repair.
Winding or grinding noises while filling or washing point to a failing pump motor or debris in the chopper. We clear or replace it.
Dishwashers that stop mid-cycle or stay stuck on drain often have a control or sensor problem. Testing narrows it down fast.
If water isn't getting hot, the heating element or thermostat has likely failed, leaving dishes wet and poorly cleaned.
A musty smell usually means food and grease are trapped in the filter or drain hose. Cleaning both clears the odor.
Door latches that won't catch keep the dishwasher from starting. Replacing the latch is one of our fastest repairs.
Built-in and drawer dishwashers are repaired in place, without pulling out your cabinets.

Detergent cups that don't open lead to dirty dishes. The dispenser latch or actuator is a quick fix.

No ice and no water from the dispenser often points to a single inlet valve. One part can fix both problems.
Ice makers that overfill and leak may have a stuck valve or a misaligned fill tube. We correct it before it damages the floor.
Freezers that run constantly but stay warm may have dirty condenser coils or a weak fan. Cleaning and a part swap usually fix it.

Commercial-style and outdoor ice machines are evaluated honestly, with a clear repair price before any work.

Disposals that are completely dead often just need the reset button pressed or the switch replaced. We check those first.
Leaks under the sink come from the flange, the dishwasher inlet or a cracked housing. We find which one.

Our [city] technicians fix disposals of every major brand, including InSinkErator models.
A disposal that smells bad usually has trapped food in the grinding chamber. Cleaning it out solves the problem.

If the disposal hums and the reset button doesn't help, the motor may be seized. We'll tell you if replacement makes sense.

Disposal switches on the wall or in the sink rim are repaired or replaced as needed.
